'''Albert Louis Allred''' (born September 19, 1931) is an American chemist accomplished in the fields of [[inorganic chemistry]] and [[electronegativity]]. He was born in [[Mount Airy, North Carolina|Mount Airy]], [[North Carolina]], United States.<ref>Geburts- und Karrieredaten nach ''American Men and Women of Science'', Thomson Gale 2004</ref>

==Education and career==
Allred studied chemistry at the [[University of North Carolina]] and earned a bachelor's degree in 1953. He studied at [[Harvard University]] and earned a master's degree in 1955, followed by a doctorate in 1957. In 1956 he was an instructor, 1958 assistant professor, and 1969 professor at the College of Arts and Sciences of [[Northwestern University]]. From 1980 to 1986, he was chairman of the chemistry department. In 1992, he became acting vice president for research as well as dean of the graduate school.{{citation needed|date=August 2026}}

In 1987, he was a visiting scholar at [[Cambridge University]], in 1965 Honorary Research Associate at University College London and in 1967 at the [[Sapienza University of Rome|University of Rome]]. From 1963 to 1965, he was a Sloan Research Fellow. He has been a Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science since 1981.{{citation needed|date=August 2026}}

Allred introduced the [[Electronegativity|Allred-Rochow scale of electronegativity]] with [[Eugene G. Rochow]] in 1958.<ref>{{Cite journal|author1=Allred, A. L. |author2=Rochow, E. G. |year=1958|journal=Journal of Inorganic and Nuclear Chemistry|volume=5|pages=264–268|doi=10.1016/0022-1902(58)80003-2|title=A scale of electronegativity based on electrostatic force|issue=4}}</ref> They predicted that electronegativity, should be related to the charge experienced by an electron on the "surface" of an atom. They calculated this formula for the electronegativity, <span class="nounderlines">''[[Chi (letter)|χ]]''</span>, where "<math> Z_{\rm eff}</math>" is equal to the [[effective nuclear charge]] and "<math>r_{\rm cov}</math>" is the [[covalent radius]]. When the covalent radius is expressed in [[picometers]]:

::<math>\chi = 3590{{Z_{\rm eff}}\over{r^2_{\rm cov}}} + 0.744</math>.

When expressed in [[Angstroms]] however, the value 3590, becomes .359.

::<math>\chi = .359{{Z_{\rm eff}}\over{r^2_{\rm cov}}} + 0.744</math>

Allred has also since dealt with synthetic inorganic, organometallic chemistry, and electrochemistry.{{citation needed|date=August 2026}}
